summary: This is a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) analysis document prepared by the SpineDAO Foundation for FILTER, an AI-driven smart appointment/triage system for spine-surgery candidates, prepared for a Molecule Labs listing. The document asserts FILTER has reached TRL 7, supported by a prospective multicenter clinical evaluation (643 patients, 7 French spine centers, NASS 2026), and outlines the remaining steps to TRL 8–9 including regulatory classification and multi-site commercial deployment.

content_blocks.title: Executive Summary — Current TRL Status
content_blocks.content: FILTER is an AI-driven smart appointment/triage system for spine-surgery candidates. Current assessed level: TRL 7 — reached. Evidence basis: (1) Prospective multicenter clinical evaluation presented at NASS 2026, Phase 2: 643 patients across 7 French spine centers, surgeons blinded to AI score. (2) Development on a retrospective cohort of 3,000+ de-identified records, peer-presented at SFCR and EUROSPINE 2025. (3) Now deploying with early surgeons in live booking workflows. (4) Commercial licence signed. Remaining steps to TRL 8–9: regulatory classification and multi-site commercial deployment.

content_blocks.title: TRL Ladder — Evidence by Level
content_blocks.content:
TRL 1–3 | Basic principles; concept; proof of concept | Clinical need defined (triage of surgical vs non-surgical spine referrals); algorithmic concept specified; Soleau priority filed | Status: Achieved
TRL 4 | Validated in the lab | Model trained and validated on 3,000+ de-identified records on the Sciencer platform; internal performance established | Status: Achieved
TRL 5 | Validated in a relevant environment | Retrospective validation against surgeons' decisions; neural-network model, ROC AUC 75.2% (SFCR 2025) | Status: Achieved
TRL 6 | Demonstrated in a relevant environment | Peer-presented at SFCR 2025 and EUROSPINE 2025; manuscript under review; IP-NFT registered on Molecule (EVM) | Status: Achieved
TRL 7 | Demonstrated in an operational environment | Prospective multicenter clinical evaluation — NASS 2026 Phase 2 (643 patients, 7 centers, blinded surgeons); now deploying with early surgeons; commercial licence signed | Status: Achieved
TRL 8 | Complete & qualified | Regulatory classification (clinical decision-support / medical-device status) per market; larger / longer-term prospective outcome data | Status: Planned
TRL 9 | Proven in operational use at scale | Multi-site commercial deployment with outcome data | Status: Planned

content_blocks.title: Basis for TRL 7 Rating — Prospective Multicenter Validation (NASS 2026, Phase 2)
content_blocks.content: Headline evidence: Prospective study across 7 French spine centers, 643 first-time lumbar patients, surgeons blinded to the AI score. Key quantitative results: FILTER showed very low potential harm (0.3%) versus 22.6% for current scheduling; reduced loss of opportunity (6–8.4% vs 37.2%) — a 7-fold reduction in missed prioritization, closely aligning with surgeon decision-making. Supporting evidence pillars: (1) Real-world data: development on 3,000+ de-identified records from clinical practice; prospective validation on 643 live first-visit patients. (2) Independent scientific scrutiny: accepted and presented at SFCR 2025, EUROSPINE 2025, and NASS 2026; Phase 2 published in The Spine Journal 26 (2026), abstract #273. (3) Operational deployment underway: in live booking workflows with early surgeons (human-in-the-loop); commercial licence signed. (4) IP protection: IP-NFT via Molecule (EVM), owned by the SpineDAO Foundation; Soleau envelope on file.

content_blocks.title: Path to TRL 8 and TRL 9
content_blocks.content: To reach TRL 8: confirm regulatory classification (clinical decision-support / medical-device status) per target market; extend prospective evidence to larger samples and longer follow-up (outcomes, not only concordance). To reach TRL 9: multi-site commercial deployment via the licensee, with prospective outcome and safety data at scale.

content_blocks.title: Honest Caveats and Limitations
content_blocks.content: The Phase 2 study is a single-arm, observational, 4-week evaluation measuring concordance and triage safety — not a randomized trial or a long-term outcomes study. Regulatory classification is not yet complete. The product is pre-revenue. FILTER is a triage decision-support aid, not an autonomous diagnostic — a clinician makes every decision. These factors bound the rating at TRL 7. Document is a TRL self-assessment prepared for the FILTER Molecule Labs listing; not legal or regulatory advice.

key_findings: FILTER assessed at TRL 7 (reached), based on a prospective multicenter clinical evaluation (NASS 2026, Phase 2: 643 patients, 7 French spine centers, surgeons blinded).
Neural-network model achieved ROC AUC 75.2% in retrospective validation against surgeon decisions (SFCR 2025).

Prospective Phase 2 results: potential harm 0.3% (FILTER) vs 22.6% (current scheduling); loss of opportunity 6–8.4% (FILTER) vs 37.2% (current scheduling) — a 7-fold reduction in missed prioritization.
Development dataset: 3,000+ de-identified records from clinical practice on the Sciencer platform.
Phase 2 results published in The Spine Journal 26 (2026), abstract #273.
Presented at SFCR 2025, EUROSPINE 2025, and NASS 2026.
Commercial licence signed; operational deployment underway with early surgeons in live booking workflows (human-in-the-loop).
IP protected via IP-NFT on Molecule (EVM) owned by SpineDAO Foundation; Soleau envelope on file.
Key limitations: single-arm observational 4-week study (not RCT), no long-term outcomes data, regulatory classification not yet complete, product is pre-revenue.
Remaining path: TRL 8 requires regulatory classification and larger/longer prospective outcome data; TRL 9 requires multi-site commercial deployment with outcome data at scale.
